title: ContextVM and canonical Nostr client migration

intended_behavior.mutations: Web and CLI client surfaces publish or document ContextVM JSON-RPC 2.0 methods over Nostr kind 25910, using CEP-4/NIP-59 encryption where supported, instead of introducing new legacy request-kind flows.
intended_behavior.reads: Client reads target canonical observable/state kinds 30900, 4903, 30315, 11316-11320, 30002, 30078 and standard NIPs, with legacy Bahia kinds retained only as migration fixtures.
intended_behavior.worker_actions: Touched worker UI paths do not hardcode legacy worker request kind numbers; legacy constants are isolated in the Nostr kind surface as migration-only constants.
intended_behavior.documentation: User-facing docs identify ContextVM method names, canonical read kinds, and backend dependencies.

out_of_scope: Server-side ContextVM method dispatcher for every legacy request family
Full removal of legacy backend subscriptions
Relay-side enforcement policy for canonical audit retention

remaining_dependencies.dependency: Backend ContextVM kind 25910 JSON-RPC handlers for service, worker, package, DNS, backup, ML, and adoption mutations
Migration documentation and PSTF verification must stay updated as backend handlers land
